text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today despite oil prices rising sharply—Brent crude jumped above $109 after Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and oil facilities on October 19th. The stock had surged $8.95 over the prior two trading days (through October 16th), so today's pullback appears to be profit-taking after that strong run rather than a reaction to deteriorating fundamentals.

The geopolitical backdrop remains supportive for oil producers: Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Iranian threats of retaliation against the U.S., and Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities are all tightening supply. The gap between U.S. crude ($101.91) and Brent ($126.55) also widened further, reflecting the premium buyers pay for oil in tighter physical markets—a setup that generally benefits integrated producers like ConocoPhillips on both production and refining.
